title: Son of God
lead: A title the Bible uses for angels, for Israel, for the king of David's line, and in the New Testament above all for Jesus. Its meaning shifts with the one it names.

sections.h: Sons of God across the Bible
sections.b: The phrase names heavenly beings (Job 1:6; Job 38:7; Genesis 6:2, debated), Israel as God's firstborn (Exodus 4:22; Hosea 11:1), and the king: God promises David's offspring, "I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to me" (2 Samuel 7:14), and the king of Psalm 2 hears, "You are my son" (Psalm 2:7; compare Psalm 89:26–27). In the New Testament Jesus is the Son of God at his baptism (Mark 1:11), in Peter's confession (Matthew 16:16) and in John's Gospel in a unique sense (John 1:14; John 1:18). Hebrews joins Psalm 2:7 and 2 Samuel 7:14 to show the Son is greater than angels (Hebrews 1:5), and Paul applies the promise to all believers as sons and daughters (2 Corinthians 6:18).
